notes: The schematic image was not visible, so the wiring is inferred from the text. It is the usual single-MOSFET 3.3V-to-5V level shifter: 2N7000 gate to 3.3V (VCC), source to the MKR data pin, drain to the NeoPixel DIN, and the 10k resistor pulling the drain up to 5V.

The catalogue entry for arduino-mkr-gsm-1400 has no digital pin ports. The data-pin jumper (wire1) therefore uses a null board port. The original example most likely uses pin 6, but that is an assumption.

Fix for the validation errors: the battery's lead ports cannot be joined to the board's BATT socket port. The battery plugs into the board through its connector, so there is now one port-less joined edge between batt1 and mkr1. The + and - electrical edges to BATT are kept.
The 2N7000 is not in the catalogue, so I added it as a new type with ports S, G and D, and a D-S channel.
The tutorial's layout shows a single NeoPixel, but the parts list names the 24-LED ring, so I used the ring. I put its PWR, GND and DIN pads directly into breadboard holes. DOUT is left unconnected.
The antenna and the micro SIM are in the setup steps but not in the parts list or the catalogue, so I left them out.
The USB cable and PC are included because the setup steps call for them.

The Gmail, Google Calendar and Google Drive MCP servers need authorization before they can be used. This session is non-interactive and could not do that. Authorize them in your claude.ai connector settings if you need them. They were not needed for this graph.
